references.text: The instruction regarding one male goat as a sin offering to the Lord, in addition to the daily burnt offering, is repeated throughout the sacrificial calendar.
The same wording concerning one male goat as a sin offering for atonement, used earlier in the chapter for the new moon day of the seventh month.
Identical wording used for the second day of the Feast of Tabernacles, showing the recurring pattern of daily sin offerings.
The same sin offering wording for the third day of the Feast of Tabernacles.
The same sin offering wording for the fourth day of the Feast of Tabernacles.
The daily burnt offering (tamid) mentioned here as the foundation to which all other offerings are added.
The basic law concerning a male goat as a sin offering, which forms the basis for the sin offering mentioned in this text.
The institution of the daily burnt offering (olat hatamid) along with its associated grain offering and drink offering.
The New Testament reflection that the repeated offerings under the law could not make worshippers perfect, pointing forward to Christ's final sacrifice.
